inputs.text: The Wisconsin case shows why protecting elections and demanding accountability from those in power must go together. Harry Wait was convicted of two misdemeanor election-fraud charges and one felony identity-theft charge, and acquitted of another identity-theft count; taking ballots in Robin Vos and Cory Mason’s names was not legitimate oversight. But officials cannot answer public doubt by insisting people simply trust the system. When institutions are opaque, they deepen suspicion and leave ordinary people with little meaningful way to challenge them. The answer is not illegal stunts or unquestioning obedience, but election rules enforced fairly and public institutions that are genuinely open to scrutiny.
